title: YOLO Mode, Safely: MicroVM Sandboxes for Any Agent — Rowan Christmas, Docker
talk_summary: A Docker PM demonstrates that coding harnesses like Claude Desktop do not actually sandbox agents: five prompts extracted browser history and bank PII, and the harness only blocks when asked directly. He pitches Docker's sbx microVM binary, which runs the agent in a separate kernel with isolated filesystem, secret-placeholder substitution on network egress, default-deny networking, and audit trails, all behind the same `sbx run claude` command.

takeaways.technique: MicroVM-per-agent-run instead of harness-level permission prompts
takeaways.what_they_do: Each agent invocation spins up a fresh microVM with its own kernel and isolated filesystem, so the agent cannot see host files (browser history, credentials) at all; the harness's 'please don't' prompts are replaced by a hard boundary.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If it gets down to your host machine, it's too late. So, you want to be at that microVM boundary.
takeaways.numbers: 5 prompts to extract browser history and bank PII from Claude Desktop; 9/10 CrowdStrike score

takeaways.technique: Secret-placeholder substitution at the network boundary
takeaways.what_they_do: The sandbox never holds real secrets; on egress the proxy swaps a placeholder for the real credential, so a compromised or confused agent cannot exfiltrate keys.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it takes a placeholder, replaces it so that your sandbox and your agent can't do bad things

takeaways.technique: Default-deny network egress with explicit allowlist
takeaways.what_they_do: Sandboxes block outbound network by default (pirate bay blocked, Anthropic telemetry blocked) and only allow configured destinations.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I tried to get it to go and look up uh the pirate bay because I I knew that would be blocked and sure enough, blocked by default.

takeaways.what_they_do: Mount adjacent codebases read-only so the agent can read context but cannot commit to repos outside its task.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I'll mount those uh, read only. That way, my agent can see what I'm doing... but I know it's not going to make random commits to other repos

takeaways.what_they_do: Track which agent did what and which human authorized it, so every action traces back to an authorizing principal; policy (Cedar) can degrade permissions based on that chain.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a human actually authorized that agent to do it. It didn't just happen by magic.
